answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce credential earned through verifiable work — a relic of past useful deeds, not a freshly spun identity. Newcomers start under a velvet glove: low trust, limited privileges, and slow reputation growth, so mass-producing fake agents costs more than it earns. A falcon-style peer audit then randomly samples new agents, cross-checking claimed work against on-chain records before granting full market access.
